title: NorthForge Onboarding Stitch-up & Runbook Huddle
next_steps: Priya to share tailored runbook and staging access checklist by 2027-09-10
Mateo to run initial perf benchmark against 2k qps baseline and share results by 2027-09-17
Jordan to send SOC2 attestation link and encryption key management notes by 2027-09-09
action_items: Priya Shah: Share onboarding runbook + sample config (due 2027-09-10)
Mateo Ruiz: Run GPU perf test (2k qps mixed seq lengths) and post results (due 2027-09-17)
Zoe Kim / NorthForge: Provide list of internal auditors and required compliance checkpoints (due 2027-09-09)
Aaron Cole: Provide staging VPC peering details and test credentials (due 2027-09-12)
summary: Kickoff for NorthForge Systems onboarding with Redwood CS/SE/AE. Main goals: validate networking/VPC plan, confirm security/compliance gating (SOC2, KMS, SSO), align on performance baseline for pilot, and agree next steps for runbook and benchmarks. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but wants cost tradeoffs and a quick hosted pilot. Action items assigned for runbook, perf tests, and security artifacts.
topics: Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
Performance baseline and benchmark plan (2k qps target)
Pilot scope: hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, welcome. Thanks for carving time today. We're here to stitch up the onboarding runbook and lock the first pilot acceptance criteria — so quick intros?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Hi this is Lena, head of infra at NorthForge. We're responsible for the platform and the hosting side.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir, platform eng manager, I'll be hands-on with the integration.
[00:17] Zoe Kim: Zoe, security, I'll own compliance gating and audit stuff.
[00:20] Mateo Ruiz: Mateo from Redwood, SE focused on runtime and perf.
[00:23] Jordan Blake: Jordan, CSM — I'll help run the onboarding cadence.
[00:26] Aaron Cole: Aaron, DevOps, I'll do the VPC work and CI hooks.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Great. Quick agenda: 1) network and access, 2) security/compliance checklist, 3) performance expectations and benchmark plan, 4) runbook handoff and timelines. Any additions?
[00:40] Maya Rivers: Maya here — project manager, timeline alignment please.
[00:43] Priya Shah: Perfect. Okay, first network. Aaron — can you recap your current staging topology?
[00:50] Aaron Cole: Yeah so we have a single VPC in us-west-2 for staging, private subnets only, NAT for egress. We prefer a VPC peering to Redwood's private endpoint or a Transit Gateway. Also we want minimal public exposure.
[01:05] Mateo Ruiz: Sounds good. Redwood supports VPC peering, TGW, and a managed private connector. For pilot we usually recommend a private endpoint + NAT egress rules so logs can talk out to SIEM. We can also run an on-prem package but that adds ops.
[01:25] Samir Patel: We're leaning to dedicated vs hosted — predictable latency. What are the real admins ops tradeoffs?
[01:31] Mateo Ruiz: Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools and throughput guarantees, so if you need 2k QPS sustained that's easiest to hit. Hosted can work for pilot if you accept variable bursts; cost usually higher per token when under load without reserved capacity. We can quantify.
[01:45] Priya Shah: We'll add a cost comparison to the runbook.
[01:48] Zoe Kim: Security piece — we need info on KMS integration, key rotation, audit logs retention. Also SSO (SAML) and RBAC mapping. Do you have SOC2?
01:58] Jordan Blake: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II — I'll share the attestation link. Also we support customer-managed keys via KMS + HSM integrations in Dedicated and Private.
[02:10] Zoe Kim: Ok, we want to see encryption-in-transit and at-rest details plus examples of audit logs — event types and retention.
[02:18] Mateo Ruiz: We keep request/response traces for a short retention by default, token-level cost breakdowns, and full audit logs in Dedicated+Private. We can send schema for logs and examples. Note slight caveat: some debug traces might include prompt hashes — we redact full prompt bodies unless you opt-in.
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: That redaction is important. For compliance we'll want hashes and pointers but not PII.
[02:41] Samir Patel: On perf — Mateo, what's your suggested baseline test? We mentioned 2k qps, but our sequences vary — some 32 tokens, some 512.
[02:50] Mateo Ruiz: Right. For realistic tests we'll run a mixed distribution: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (64-256), 10% long (256-1024). We'll run cpus and GPUs? — sorry, typo — we'll run on GPU clusters. We'll exercise batching, KV cache behavior, and quantized model variants.
[03:10] Aaron Cole: Will you mock upstream latency? Our real apps have a 40–80ms preprocessing step.
[03:15] Mateo Ruiz: We can add synthetic upstream latency to mirror your pipeline. Also we'll test cold vs warm KV cache to show tail latencies.
[03:24] Priya Shah: Mateo, estimate for running the perf run and a short report?
[03:28] Mateo Ruiz: I can get initial numbers within a week of having staging credentials — so target 2027-09-17.
[03:33] Maya Rivers: That timeline is fine.
[03:35] Zoe Kim: For KMS we need process docs on key rotation and where keys are kept if you support customer-managed keys for Private.
[03:42] Jordan Blake: We'll attach KMS integration notes. For Private, you bring your KMS or HSM and we integrate over mutual TLS. For Dedicated we have optional bring-your-own-key modes.
[03:54] Samir Patel: Any blockers for us to do a quick hosted pilot while Dedicated procurement happens?
[03:58] Priya Shah: You can do a hosted pilot quickly. It gives you fast data but no pinned commits. We recommend hosted pilot for functional validation and Dedicated for performance production.
[04:10] Lena Ortiz: Ok, what's the expected time to get staging access?
[04:13] Jordan Blake: If we have the network info, we can provision a staging endpoint in 2 business days.
[04:18] Aaron Cole: I'll share VPC CIDRs and a contact for peering.
[04:22] Priya Shah: Great. Onboarding runbook — we'll share a living doc that includes: checklist for networking, SSO setup steps, KMS config, sample IAM/RBAC mapping, benchmark scripts, and a rollback plan.
[04:36] Samir Patel: We also want runbook steps for canary rollouts and A/B test between quantized and full model.
[04:42] Mateo Ruiz: We'll include model variant recommendations and automatic fallback policies. We'll also show batching and cache configs that trade cost vs latency.
[04:52] Zoe Kim: Auditability: we need to know how long logs live by default and retention options. Also any e-discovery support?
[04:58] Jordan Blake: Default retention for request logs is 30 days on hosted; you can extend on Dedicated/Private. We have export hooks for SIEM and long-term storage. E-discovery support is through log exports and search indexes.
[05:12] Priya Shah: Quick aside on quotas — you'll hit rate limits if using hosted. We can pre-configure higher quotas on pilot. For Dedicated we give throughput SLAs.
[05:22] Lena Ortiz: Pricing — can you share an example invoice for a 3-month pilot and a separate Dedicated commit?
[05:28] Priya Shah: Yes, I'll get a tailored pricing sheet. We'll include token cost, reserved capacity pricing, and burst fees.
[05:34] Samir Patel: Anything on network egress costs?
[05:36] Mateo Ruiz: Egress depends on your cloud region. If peering, egress is minimized; we'll include rough numbers for us-west-2.
[05:42] Maya Rivers: Let's talk success criteria for pilot so we can sign off.
[05:46] Priya Shah: Proposal: functional correctness (>=95% pass on a 50-case eval suite), latency P95 under 180ms for short requests in warm cache, throughput sustaining 2k QPS with target token mix, and security signoffs (SOC2 docs + KMS details). Thoughts?
[06:02] Samir Patel: P95 180ms seems fair for short requests if Dedicated. For hosted pilot we might see higher tails but still useful.
[06:10] Zoe Kim: Security signoff depends on review of audit logs and KMS flows.
[06:14] Aaron Cole: We'll also look at how rollout behaves with our CI/CD.
[06:18] Priya Shah: We'll include CI examples in runbook.
[06:21] [07:45] Mateo Ruiz: quick note — sometimes transcripts say KV cache as K-V chache — internal joke — but we will ensure proper docs.
[07:52] Samir Patel: ha noted.
[07:54] [12:00] Jordan Blake: I'll send over SOC2 link and a brief of network template. Also adding the attestation and the redacted sample logs.
[12:07] Zoe Kim: For audit logs, please show which fields are present.
[12:12] Jordan Blake: Will do.
[12:15] [20:05] Aaron Cole: I'll open a ticket with the peering details and an owner.
[20:10] Maya Rivers: I'll put the timeline into our PM tracker.
[20:15] Priya Shah: Recap — action items: Priya share runbook + pricing, Mateo run perf tests, Jordan share SOC2 + logs, Aaron share VPC details, Zoe to confirm compliance checklist.
[20:30] Samir Patel: Sounds good. Any concerns about staffing? We might need an SE on call during the first week of pilot.
[20:36] Mateo Ruiz: I can be on standby for the pilot week. We'll also schedule a focused troubleshooting slot.
[20:42] Lena Ortiz: Budget approval — procurement will need the cost sheet for our finance team.
[20:46] Priya Shah: We'll get that to you with clear line items.
[20:50] [34:00] Jordan Blake: I'll schedule the pilot validation call for 2027-09-20 and send calendar invites.
[34:06] Maya Rivers: Tentatively blocked.
[34:10] [45:00] Zoe Kim: One last thing on compliance: do you have an incident response playbook for Dedicated/private?
[45:08] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we have incident response runbooks — we will include summary and contact escalation matrix in the runbook. For Private deployments you get tight SLAs and direct pager.
[45:22] Aaron Cole: Good to know.
[45:25] Priya Shah: Any final Qs?
[45:28] Samir Patel: None from me.
[45:30] Lena Ortiz: All good.
[45:33] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and the perf plan.
[58:00] Meeting end: informal chatter and goodbyes.
